headline: Mark reachable prefix boundaries
statement: Determine whether the entire string s can be segmented into one or more words from wordDict. A dictionary word may be reused as often as needed.
constraints: Each dictionary word has 1 to 20 lowercase letters
s is lowercase and dictionary words are unique
intuition: Imagine boundaries between characters. Boundary end is reachable if an earlier reachable boundary start is followed by a dictionary word. A valid segmentation reaches the final boundary; a locally longest word is not always the right choice.
approach: Convert wordDict to a set and record the maximum word length.
Set dp[0] true for the empty prefix.
For each end, try reachable starts no farther than the longest word; mark dp[end] true on a match.
correctness: Induct on end. A successful transition appends one dictionary word to a valid prefix, yielding a valid segmentation. Conversely the last word of any valid segmentation starts at a reachable earlier boundary considered by the transition. Thus dp describes all and only segmentable prefixes.
bruteForce: Recursively try every next dictionary word without memoization. Repeatedly exploring the same suffix can take exponential time.

complexity.explanation: n=len(s), L is the maximum dictionary word length, and D is the total number of dictionary characters. At most L candidate slices of length up to L are created and hashed per boundary; DP storage is O(n) and the dictionary uses O(D) as an upper bound.

pitfalls: A word may be reused; do not remove it after matching.
Greedy longest-prefix matching can miss a valid segmentation.
True for a short prefix does not guarantee true for the entire string.
